title: Nailing the Hookpoint
coreMove: Land the concentrated moment where the room can feel why the offer matters now.
sourcePressure: Hookpoint chapter: after frame, story, intrigue, and prize have prepared the room, the pitch needs a concentrated peak where novelty, consequence, and desire converge.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must keep hookpoint as the peak created by prior sequence, not a slogan, line, or clever headline pasted onto weak material.

hook: Every pitch needs a killer line
counterintuition: A slogan is not a peak

exampleSpecs.domain: battery-recycling company pitching a closed-loop supply deal to an electric bus manufacturer
exampleSpecs.audience: a commercial lead whose value case is spread across compliance, cost, and supply security
exampleSpecs.stakes: the manufacturer misses the immediate value unless one moment shows the next battery order at risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after tracing supply risk, she reveals the purchase order the manufacturer cannot fill without recycled cobalt and lets the room connect timing to value
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a redacted purchase order beside a vial of black battery powder

exampleSpecs.domain: regional theater director pitching a corporate ticket block for a new production
exampleSpecs.audience: an arts leader who must make business buyers feel why the production matters now
exampleSpecs.stakes: the buyer sees hospitality spend instead of a timely employee-retention tool
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she waits until after the workforce story, then shows the scene title that mirrors the buyer's retention crisis and stops speaking
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rehearsal script opened to a scene title beside a corporate badge

exampleSpecs.domain: precision irrigation firm pitching a citrus cooperative before a drought allocation vote
exampleSpecs.audience: a sales engineer whose facts are scattered across water, yield, and hardware
exampleSpecs.stakes: growers vote on allocations before seeing the one number that makes delay expensive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he reveals the acre-feet saved per night only after growers have seen the allocation calendar, then asks who wants that number before the vote
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an irrigation valve tag lying on a paper drought calendar

exampleSpecs.domain: documentary distributor pitching a streaming platform on a regional investigation series
exampleSpecs.audience: a distributor trying to concentrate audience, urgency, and exclusivity into one peak
exampleSpecs.stakes: the platform treats the series as one more nonfiction title unless the release window matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she holds back the whistleblower interview clip until after the competitor schedule, then plays the first ten seconds and names the embargo date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a timecoded interview still on a laptop beside an embargo letter

exampleSpecs.domain: advanced prosthetics clinic presenting a microprocessor knee to veterans' benefits reviewers
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician whose data needs one peak of human and financial consequence
exampleSpecs.stakes: reviewers approve cheaper equipment that costs independence and later care dollars
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after showing gait data, she plays eight seconds of the patient stepping off a curb without help and then shows the avoided-care total
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a prosthetic knee joint beside a paused curb-step video

exampleSpecs.domain: craft paper mill pitching compostable packaging to a fast-casual restaurant chain
exampleSpecs.audience: a mill sales lead trying to make packaging consequence converge with brand risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: the chain delays while a city ordinance deadline approaches
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the team to picture opening week under the new ordinance, then reveals their current wrapper on the banned-material list
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded takeout wrapper beside a city ordinance notice

skillTargets: identify whether the peak follows sufficient setup
choose a hookpoint that concentrates consequence and desire
analyze scattered facts versus one peak moment
evaluate hookpoints that are slogans without stakes

tryThisNowSpec: Name the one moment in your pitch where value, timing, and consequence should meet, then move any early facts that weaken that peak.
